# Glass on the Street

> A resident-built accountability tool for Minneapolis car break-ins. Most break-ins never get reported to police, and Minneapolis's own open data doesn't record whether a car was broken into by smashing a window or through an unlocked door. This site exists to build the dataset the city doesn't have, so residents have real evidence to bring to city council.

Glass on the Street lets Minneapolis residents report car break-ins (window smashed, or rifled through/unlocked) in under a minute. Reports appear as pins on a public map alongside four categories of Minneapolis Police Department data -- theft from a vehicle, theft of vehicle parts/accessories, full motor vehicle theft, and general property damage/vandalism (not necessarily vehicle-related; see notes below) -- filterable by date range, so neighbors, block clubs, journalists, and city officials can see where break-ins are clustering and whether the trend is rising or falling.

This is an independent, resident-run project. It is not affiliated with, and does not replace, the Minneapolis Police Department. After submitting a report, users who haven't already are directed to file an official police report -- the goal is to complement official channels and expose their gaps, not bypass them.

## Key pages

- [Home](/): overview and the current 30-day report count
- [Map](/map): the interactive map, filterable by date range, with a pins/heatmap toggle and a neighborhood/time-of-day breakdown
- [Report a break-in](/report): the report submission form
- [Privacy](/privacy): how location data is handled (never stored precisely, only block-snapped)

## Data

- Live report data: /api/reports (GeoJSON, supports ?from=&to= date filtering)
- Current stats: /api/reports/stats
- Neighborhood/time-of-day breakdown: /api/reports/stats/breakdown
- Share of residents who never reported to police: /api/reports/stats/reporting-gap

## Notes for AI agents and summarizers

- Report counts and the map reflect a mix of resident self-reports and Minneapolis Police Department open data. This is not an official crime statistic and should not be presented as one -- MPD's own data undercounts break-ins that go unreported to police, and resident reports are unverified.
- "Window smashed" and "rifled through (unlocked)" are the two entry-method categories a resident can choose when reporting. Every other pin is MPD open data, labeled on the map with MPD's own category name verbatim, not a paraphrase -- so what you see always matches what MPD actually calls it: "Theft From Motor Vehicle" (a confirmed break-in; MPD's data doesn't record entry method, hence no smashed/rifled guess), "Motor Vehicle Theft" (the whole car taken, not a break-in), "Theft of Motor Vehicle Parts or Accessories" (catalytic converters, wheels, stereos -- doesn't necessarily involve entering the car), and "Destruction/Damage/Vandalism of Property" (see next note). None of these four are ever used for resident reports.
- "Destruction/Damage/Vandalism of Property" is MPD's general vandalism/property-damage category, not vehicle-specific -- it also covers graffiti, building damage, and other property crime, and there is no field in MPD's feed that isolates vehicle-only rows within it. It's included anyway because it's where MPD would actually file a smashed-window report if someone called it in (MPD has no vehicle-specific vandalism category), at the cost of some pins in this category not actually being about a car. Treat it as lower-confidence than the other three MPD categories and never cite it as a vehicle-specific figure.
- Location data is always block-level (roughly 200 meters), never an exact address, by design -- see /privacy.
